how.question: How does a SaaS affiliate program work?
how.answer: Each affiliate gets a link. {brand} records the click, ties the visitor to the payment they later make on Stripe and calculates the commission with your program's rule — renewals included.

checkout.question: Do I have to change my checkout?
checkout.answer: Not with Payment Links: the tracker tag is enough. With Stripe Checkout it is one extra field when you create the session; with a custom checkout or the Subscriptions API, one metadata key.

stripe.question: Does it work with Stripe?
stripe.answer: Yes. Stripe is the stable payment method today: commissions are calculated from the payments, refunds and disputes it sends by webhook. Other methods are still being validated.

calculation.question: How are commissions calculated?
calculation.answer: A percentage or a fixed amount per paid invoice, once or recurring for a number of months or for life. Every commission keeps the rule that produced it, and a refund creates a reversal.

money.question: Does {brand} move any money?
money.answer: No. {brand} calculates and records what you owe each affiliate; you pay them from your own account, the way you already do.

fee.question: Do you take a percentage of my revenue?
fee.answer: No. You pay a fixed monthly fee for the tool — no percentage and no revenue cap. See <pricing>pricing</pricing>.

providers.question: My SaaS uses more than one payment method. Do I integrate each one separately?
providers.answer: No. Tracking and customer identity are set up once. Then you connect the billing accounts you use. In checkouts without sign-up, the attribution reference may need to travel to the payment.

prerequisites.title: Before you start

items.program: An active program (Programs → New program). Fill in the product website so affiliates get the default link.
items.affiliate: At least one approved affiliate — only approved participations earn commissions.
items.keys: The test public key and secret key, generated in Integrations. Live keys come later, with an active plan.
items.stripe: Access to your payment method's dashboard — on Stripe, with permission to create webhook endpoints.
items.access: Access to your site's HTML and your backend code.

prerequisites.keysOnceBody: A key is only displayed when it is generated. Keep the secret one in a secrets manager; if you lose it, generate a new one (the previous key stops working immediately).
prerequisites.lead: Estimated time: about 15 minutes in test mode, with the access below at hand.

installTracker.title: Install the tracker on your site
installTracker.lead: Paste the tag before {head}. The tracker is a small {brand} script: it reads the affiliate's code from the URL, creates the visitor id and records the click.

facts.whereValue: Before {head} on the pages affiliates link to and on your sign-up page — that is where visitorId is read.
facts.keyValue: Your publishable key in the data-key attribute: pk_test_… while you validate, pk_live_… in production.
facts.sendsValue: Only when the URL has a referral code: POST /api/track with the publishable key, the code, the visitorId, the URL, the referrer and the utm_* parameters.

details.params: Looks for the referral code in the <params></params> URL parameters.
details.cookie: Stores a visitor id (v_…) in the {cookie} cookie on your own domain for {days} days, with SameSite=Lax (and Secure over HTTPS). Browsers with tracking prevention, such as Safari, may shorten that to about 7 days.
details.send: When the URL has a code, sends the click to /api/track.
details.noRef: Without a code in the URL it only renews the cookie — nothing is sent. On every page it exposes window.Referral.visitorId.
details.subdomain: To share the cookie across subdomains (visit on www., sign-up on app.), add data-cookie-domain="yoursite.com" to the tag.

expected.ok: Open https://yoursite.com/?ref=CODE with the code of an approved affiliate in a test program. Under Affiliates, that affiliate's Clicks column goes up, and in the browser console window.Referral.visitorId returns v_….
expected.check: Nothing? In the browser's Network tab, check the /api/track response and look the code up in Errors.

checkoutMethods.title: Stripe checkout reference
checkoutMethods.lead: Only for guest checkout, or when the Stripe customer is created by the checkout itself. The tracker keeps an attribution reference in the browser — an opaque value only {brand} can resolve. Pick only the path you use below.

facts.valueValue: window.Referral.attributionToken, exposed on any page with the tracker installed.
facts.organicValue: The reference is null when the visitor did not come through an affiliate. Send it anyway: a payment with no reference is recorded normally, simply without a commission.
facts.renewalValue: You send the reference once. Renewals follow the customer that is already bound — there is nothing to repeat.

hosted.title: Stripe Checkout
hosted.body: One line when you create the session: client_reference_id. It is the field Stripe itself reserves for your own reference, and it arrives on the checkout.session.completed event.

links.title: Payment Links
links.body: No code at all. The tracker finds the buy.stripe.com links on the page and appends the reference itself. A link that already carries a client_reference_id is left alone.
links.calloutTitle: The payment needs a Stripe customer
links.calloutBody: For Payment Links and one-off Checkout, turn on customer_creation: always. A payment with no Stripe customer never enters the ledger and earns nothing — that shows up under Integrations, not in the Stripe dashboard.

custom.title: Custom checkout (Elements / PaymentIntent)
custom.body: One key in the PaymentIntent's metadata. Nothing else about your checkout changes.

subscriptions.title: Subscriptions API
subscriptions.body: If you create the Customer and Subscription straight through Stripe's API, put the reference in the subscription's metadata, once.

expected.ok: After a test purchase the conversion shows under Conversions with the right affiliate, and the commission under Commissions — with no call to your backend beyond the one you already made to charge.

identifyCustomer.title: Identify the customer at signup
identifyCustomer.optionalTitle: The step that makes {brand} independent of the payment method
identifyCustomer.optionalBody: Once the customer is identified, the referral belongs to the customer, not to a checkout. This is the recommended path — see Customer-first. The checkout reference is still supported for charging before any signup exists (guest checkout).
identifyCustomer.lead: A click alone earns nothing. Identify links the anonymous visitor to the customer in your system — that link is how a payment, through any connected method, reaches the affiliate.
identifyCustomer.securityTitle: Never send your secret key to the browser
identifyCustomer.securityBody: Do not call /api/identify from the front end. The route deliberately sends no CORS headers: the browser blocks any call carrying Authorization at the preflight and never lets JavaScript read the response. A customer id coming from the browser would let anyone divert commissions.
identifyCustomer.visitorIdBody: The tracker writes the {cookie} cookie on your site's domain. If sign-up is served from the same domain, the cookie arrives with your server's request. If it is on a subdomain, use data-cookie-domain on the tracker tag. If your backend is on another domain, copy window.Referral.visitorId into the sign-up form.
identifyCustomer.stripeIdTitle: How the payment finds the customer again
identifyCustomer.stripeIdBody: A Stripe payment finds the affiliate through the Stripe customer id. Without it, it uses the e-mail sent to identify, compared with the payment's e-mail (the customer's on an invoice, or a one-off payment's receipt_email when it has a customer). On the first payment matched by e-mail the Stripe id is saved, and later payments match by it. If you call identify before creating the Stripe customer, send the e-mail on that first call: it is how the payment finds the customer again. The payment must have a Stripe customer: without one it is not recorded — for Payment Links and one-off Checkout, turn on customer_creation: always. With a customer but no matching id or e-mail, it is recorded without a commission. Both cases answer Stripe with 200: the loss shows up under Integrations, not in the Stripe dashboard.

facts.whenValue: Right after you create the user's account. Call again when you create the Stripe customer, to send providerCustomerId — the same externalId updates the same customer.
facts.whereValue: Only from your backend: a route handler, server action, API or job.

responseFields.customerId: customerId — the customer's id in {brand}. The same externalId returns the same id.
responseFields.attributionsBound: attributionsBound — how many of this visitor's attributions are linked to this customer: the open ones this call linked plus those already theirs.

identifyCustomer.responseErrors: On error the response carries error with a stable code and the matching HTTP status — see Errors.

expected.ok: 200 with attributionsBound above zero — one per program — for a visitor who arrived through ?ref=. Repeating the call for the same customer returns the same number.
expected.zero: 0 means there was no open attribution for that visitorId in this environment: the visitor never came through an affiliate link, the window expired, the visitorId sent is not the cookie's, the attribution already belongs to another customer, or the key is from the other environment.

fields.name: Field
fields.visitorId: Id created by the tracker: v_ followed by 16 to 48 lowercase letters or digits.
fields.externalId: The user's id in your system (1 to 200 characters). Calls with the same value update the same customer.
fields.providerCustomerId: The customer's id at the payment method — cus_… on Stripe, up to 200 characters (the format is not validated). The most direct way to tie payments to the affiliate.
fields.email: The customer's e-mail, stored only as a hash. Without providerCustomerId, it is how a Stripe payment finds the customer — send the address Stripe has.
fields.provider: The payment method the providerCustomerId belongs to: stripe (default), mercado_pago, abacatepay or asaas. Call identify again with another method to register the same customer's identity there.

connectStripe.title: Stripe
connectStripe.lead: Under Integrations → Payments → Add payment method → Stripe. When the Authorize on Stripe button shows, just authorize: {brand} receives the events with no key and no secret to paste.

account.title: Enter your Stripe account
account.body: Under Integrations, enter your Stripe account ID (acct_…). It is in the Stripe dashboard, under Settings → Account details.

endpoint.title: Create the endpoint in Stripe
endpoint.body: In the Stripe dashboard, under Developers → Webhooks, add an endpoint with the URL Integrations shows — it ends with your integration's ID. When creating it:

checklist.customer: For Payment Links and one-off Checkout, turn on customer_creation: always — a payment without a Stripe customer earns no commission.

events.title: Select the events
events.body: Select these {count} events — invoice_payment.paid is required: it is what links the invoice to the payment and prevents a double commission. What each one records is under Stripe events.

secret.title: Paste the signing secret
secret.body: On the endpoint's page, reveal the signing secret (whsec_…) and paste it into Integrations, in the field for that mode — test or live. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.

confirm.title: Send a test event
confirm.body: Resend an event from the endpoint in the Stripe dashboard, or use the Stripe CLI:

connectStripe.modesTitle: One URL, one endpoint per mode
connectStripe.modesBody: Use the same URL in Stripe's test and live modes; each mode has its own endpoint and its own secret. Each event's livemode decides where it goes, and an event signed with the other mode's secret is rejected. See Test and live.

notes.idempotent: Redeliveries never duplicate a commission. Each event is recorded once; resending an event already recorded answers 200 and does nothing again.
notes.retry: Failures are retried. If recording fails, the endpoint answers 500 and Stripe retries automatically.
notes.currency: Program currency. A payment only earns a commission in the program's currency: a BRL program records a USD payment, but without a commission.

expected.ok: Integrations shows Receiving events with the time of the last event. If the test payment did not come from an affiliate click, the badge reads Receiving, no commission — that is expected.
expected.check: If it shows Signature rejected, the pasted secret belongs to another endpoint or the other mode. The codes the endpoint returns are under Errors.

facts.needValue: Connect the account and authorize read access to payments. When authorization is not available, use the manual setup below (3 steps in the Stripe dashboard).
facts.doesValue: Receives the events, reads each one in the same shape as any method, links the payment to the customer, records the transaction and sends it to the commission calculation.
facts.supportedValue: Subscriptions and renewals, one-off payments, full and partial refunds, disputes — including won ones, which give the commission back —, test and live, multiple accounts.
facts.limitsValue: A payment without a Stripe customer does not enter the ledger: on Payment Links and one-off Checkout, turn on customer_creation: always. Declined payments are not read. A commission already paid is not clawed back on a refund — see Refunds.
facts.testValue: In Stripe's test mode, pay with card 4242 4242 4242 4242 or run stripe trigger invoice.paid.

connectStripe.manualLead: Only when the Authorize on Stripe button does not show: you create the events endpoint in the Stripe dashboard and paste its secret into {brand}.

commission.title: How the commission is calculated
commission.lead: On a 30% program, a confirmed payment earns the commission below for the affiliate who owns the attribution.
commission.conditionsTitle: A commission is only earned when

conditions.approved: the affiliate's participation in the program is approved;
conditions.currency: the payment is in the program's currency;
conditions.amount: the payment amount is above zero;
conditions.window: the first payment happens within the attribution window;
conditions.duration: renewals happen within the program's duration (first payment only, N months or for as long as the customer pays).

lifecycle.pending: Pending — created on payment. Stays so until the payment date plus the hold period; with a 0-day hold it starts Available.
lifecycle.available: Available — the hold is over; it can go into a payout batch.
lifecycle.approved: In a batch — in a batch awaiting payment. Cancelling the batch returns it to Available.
lifecycle.paid: Paid — the batch was marked as paid.
lifecycle.reversed: Reversed — a refund or dispute creates a proportional negative row. A full refund of an unpaid commission marks it Reversed; a commission already paid is not clawed back from the affiliate. If the dispute is won, the reversed amount comes back as Pending, serving the hold again from the date the dispute closed — unless the commission had already been paid, in which case nothing comes back. Nothing is deleted.

units.money: Money is kept in the currency's minor units: {minor} = {amount}.
units.rounding: The maths runs in minor units and rounds half-up (0.5 always to the larger absolute value). Reversals use exact integer arithmetic.
units.fixed: Flat-amount programs store an empty commission_rate and pay the flat amount per payment, even when it exceeds the payment. A custom rate set for an affiliate replaces the program's.

verify.title: Test the integration
verify.lead: Walk the whole path with a test affiliate, with Test data on in the dashboard. Each step depends on the one before: stop at the first that fails.

click.title: Click recorded
click.where: Affiliates, Clicks column, after opening your site with ?ref= and the affiliate's code.
click.ifNot: the tracker did not load on that page, the code does not exist in a test program (404) or data-key is invalid (401).

identify.title: Customer identified
identify.where: the identify response, with attributionsBound above zero; the Overview funnel counts the sign-up.
identify.ifNot: the visitorId sent is not the visitor's cookie, the secret key is a live one, or the attribution window expired.

webhook.title: Payment received
webhook.where: Integrations → Payments: the account goes from Waiting for events to Healthy after a test payment (on Stripe, card 4242 4242 4242 4242).
webhook.ifNot: open the account under Payments: the Needs attention section says what is missing — endpoint, events, secret or key.

commission.title: Commission created
commission.where: Commissions shows the commission as Pending, and Conversions shows the payment with the affiliate.
commission.ifNot: the payment has no Stripe customer, providerCustomerId or the e-mail did not match the identified customer, the affiliate is not approved, or the currency differs from the program's.

verify.doneBody: A pending commission under Commissions means click, identification, webhook and calculation all worked end to end.

attribution.title: Attribution
attribution.lead: Attribution is the link between a visitor and the affiliate who gets credit for them. It decides who earns the commission when the visitor becomes a customer and pays. Each program has its own attributions; if the same customer is attributed in more than one program, a payment still earns a single commission.

facts.startsValue: On a click with a referral code, when the program is active and the affiliate's participation is approved. Clicks on programs that are not active (draft, paused or archived) are recorded but neither create nor change attributions.
facts.binds: When it links to a customer
facts.bindsValue: When your server calls identify with the visitorId, while the attribution is open.
facts.paysValue: On the first payment within the window, then on renewals within the program's duration.
facts.configValue: The model (first or last click) and the window, per program, under Programs. New programs start with last click and 60 days.

attribution.windowBody: The window is how many days the attribution stays open after the click — 1 to 365, per program. The sign-up and the first payment must both happen before it closes.

click.title: Click with ?ref=
click.note: The attribution opens and stays valid until day 60.

signup.title: Sign-up — your server calls identify
signup.note: The attribution is linked to the customer.

payment.title: First payment
payment.note: Within the window: earns the commission.

renewal.title: Renewal
renewal.note: The window has closed, but renewals follow the program's duration, not the window.

attribution.windowNote: Had the first payment happened on day 61, there would be no commission. The example uses 60 days, the default for new programs; the real value is the one set on the program.
attribution.modelsLead: The model decides what happens when the same visitor clicks different affiliates' links while the window is open.
attribution.firstClickBody: The first affiliate keeps the attribution for as long as the window opened on day 1 lasts. B's click is recorded but does not change the credit. Once the window closes, the next click opens a new attribution — in both models.
attribution.lastClickBody: The most recent click takes the attribution, and the window restarts from day 3. This is the default for new programs.
attribution.lockTitle: After sign-up, the affiliate does not change
attribution.lockBody: Once identify links the visitor to a customer, another affiliate's click no longer moves the credit, under either model. The click is still recorded.

pause.title: Paused program
pause.lead: Pausing a program stops new attributions. Customers already attributed keep following the existing commission rules until their eligibility ends.

items.clicks: New clicks still show in reports, but neither create nor change attributions.
items.before: Referrals made before the pause stay valid until the window expires: someone who clicked before and signs up during the pause still goes to the affiliate.
items.customers: Customers already attributed earn commissions as usual while the other rules hold — window, duration, approved affiliate, currency and environment.
items.archived: Draft and archived follow the same rule: only an active program creates attributions.

holdPeriod.title: Hold period
holdPeriod.body: How many days a commission stays Pending before it can be paid. It covers refunds: if the payment is refunded during this period, the commission is reversed before anyone is paid. Do not confuse it with the attribution window — one decides whether there is a commission, the other decides when it can be paid.

controls.label: Decides
controls.window: Whether the payment earns a commission for the affiliate

starts.label: Counts from
starts.window: The click (with last click, restarts on every new click)

after.label: When it ends
after.window: A first payment after it earns no commission
after.hold: The commission moves from Pending to Available

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.lead: Each workspace has two kinds of key, each in test and live. A test key never reaches a live program, and vice versa.

uses.clicks: Records clicks and visitor attributions; it never reads workspace data.

uses.env: In environment variables — never in the repository or the browser bundle.

apiKeys.exposeBody: No secret key in the browser, in Client Components, in NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables, in public bundles or in your repository. Whoever holds the secret key can link customers to affiliates in your workspace.

facts.generate: Where to generate: under Integrations, per environment.
facts.once: Shown once: each key only appears when it is generated. Keep the secret one in a secrets manager.
facts.rotate: Generating a new key invalidates the old one immediately. Update the tracker (publishable key) or the server variable (secret key) right after.

identifyApi.title: Identify API
identifyApi.authValue: Authorization: Bearer sk_test_… or sk_live_…. Secret key only; a publishable key gets 401.
identifyApi.rateLimitValue: {count} requests per minute per IP; above that, 429 with a Retry-After header.
identifyApi.idempotencyValue: Safe: the same externalId updates the same customer, without erasing a stored providerCustomerId or e-mail.

webhookEvents.title: Stripe events
webhookEvents.lead: Select these events on the webhook endpoint. Any other event is accepted with 200 and ignored.

types.checkoutReference: Checkout completed → binds the referral to the Stripe customer (this is what makes identify optional); records no money
types.payment: Invoice payment → may earn a commission
types.oneOffPayment: One-off payment (no invoice) → may earn a commission
types.refund: Refund, partial included → proportional commission reversal
types.chargeback: Dispute → reversal proportional to the disputed amount
types.disputeWon: Dispute won or inquiry closed → the reversed commission comes back, on hold (a lost dispute changes nothing)
types.paymentLink: Links the invoice to the payment that paid it → refunds and disputes find the commission

errors.title: Errors
errors.lead: The APIs answer with JSON {json} and the matching HTTP status. The error field is stable; some responses also carry message, in English, for debugging only.

identify.title: POST /api/identify
identify.lead: Called by your server. Codes are listed in the order the route checks them.

rate_limited.cause: About 120 requests per minute from the same IP — short bursts are tolerated.
rate_limited.fix: Wait the Retry-After seconds; do not call in a loop.

invalid_payload.cause: The body is not JSON, visitorId or externalId is missing, or a field has an invalid type, length or format.
invalid_payload.fix: Check the body against the Fields table.

unauthorized.cause: The key is malformed, revoked, replaced by a new one, or publishable.
unauthorized.fix: Use the current secret key of the right environment.

validation_error.fix: Send the user's id in your system.

LIVE_MODE_REQUIRED.cause: An sk_live_… key without an active Launch or Growth plan.
LIVE_MODE_REQUIRED.fix: Use the test key or activate a plan with live mode.

SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED.cause: A live key with the subscription overdue past the grace period.

internal_error.cause: An unexpected failure on our side.
internal_error.fix: Retry with backoff; repeating identify is safe.

identify.label: POST /api/identify

track.title: POST /api/track · tracker
track.lead: Called by the tracker in the browser; you see the responses in the Network tab. Success is 200 with attributed: false when the click was recorded without an attribution (paused program or affiliate not approved).

rate_limited.cause: About 60 clicks per minute from the same IP — short bursts are tolerated.
rate_limited.fix: Nothing to do under normal traffic; the limit guards against abuse.

invalid_payload.cause: A request outside the tracker's contract — for example a page URL longer than 2000 characters.
invalid_payload.fix: Use the Install the tracker tag unchanged and avoid very long landing URLs.

invalid_ref.cause: The code in the URL has an invalid format: 2 to 49 characters, starting with a letter or digit, followed by letters, digits, - or _ (uppercase is lowercased). Over 64 characters the answer is invalid_payload.

invalid_visitor.cause: The visitorId sent does not follow the v_… format. The tracker replaces an invalid cookie by itself, so this only happens on requests made outside it.
invalid_visitor.fix: Use the tag from Install the tracker, unmodified.

unknown_key.cause: data-key does not exist, was replaced by a new key, or is a secret key.
unknown_key.fix: Put the current publishable key in data-key.

not_found.cause: No affiliate has that code in a program of this environment.
not_found.fix: Check the code and that the key (test or live) matches the program's environment.

no_content.cause: A pk_live_… key without live mode: nothing is recorded.
no_content.fix: Activate a plan with live mode or use the test key.

internal_error.cause: An unexpected failure on our side.

track.label: POST /api/track (tracker)

webhook.title: Stripe webhook · POST /api/webhooks/stripe/:id
webhook.lead: What the endpoint answers Stripe. You see it under Developers → Webhooks → the endpoint's deliveries.

not_found.cause: The ID in the URL is wrong, or the integration has no saved secret yet.
not_found.fix: Copy the URL from Integrations and paste the signing secret.

missing_signature.cause: A request without the Stripe-Signature header — it did not come from Stripe.
missing_signature.fix: Send events from Stripe or the Stripe CLI.

invalid_signature.cause: The saved secret is not this endpoint's, or the event's mode has no saved secret yet.
invalid_signature.fix: Paste this endpoint's secret into the right mode's field.

livemode_mismatch.cause: A live event signed with the test secret, or the reverse.
livemode_mismatch.fix: Paste each secret into its own mode's field.

processing_failed.cause: The event arrived but recording it failed.
processing_failed.fix: Stripe resends on its own; if it keeps failing, contact support.

ignored.cause: An event not on the list, or a live event without an active plan (live_mode_inactive).
ignored.fix: For live events, resend from Stripe after activating the plan.

webhook.label: Stripe webhook

environments.title: Test and live
environments.lead: Every program is born in test or in live and never changes. Both live in the same workspace but never mix: test events never reach live programs, and test clicks, customers and commissions never enter the live ledger. The API URL and the webhook URL are the same for both.

use.label: For
use.test: Validating the integration, no real money

plan.label: Plan
plan.live: Active Launch or Growth (trial and the 7-day grace period included)

environments.withoutLiveTitle: Without a plan with live mode

withoutLive.track: /api/track with a live key answers 204 and records nothing.
withoutLive.identify: /api/identify with a live key answers 402 with LIVE_MODE_REQUIRED.
withoutLive.webhook: Live Stripe events are acknowledged but neither processed nor recorded — resend them from the Stripe dashboard after activating the plan.

environments.simulateBody: On a test program's page, “Simulate conversion” runs the whole path — click, identify and payment — through the same services as the real integration, and can also simulate a renewal and a refund.

plan.title: Activate a plan with live mode
plan.body: Live mode is part of the Launch and Growth plans. If payment is more than 7 days overdue, live processing stops (SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED).

program.title: Create the live program
program.body: Under Programs → New program, choose live — you can copy the settings of a test program — and invite the affiliates who will sell; anyone you invite is approved straight away. A test program never changes environment.

keys.title: Generate the live keys
keys.body: Under Integrations, generate the live publishable and secret keys. Each is shown only once.

swap.title: Swap the keys in your code
swap.body: In the tracker, use pk_live_… in data-key. On the server, point the environment variable at the sk_live_… key.

stripe.title: Create the endpoint in Stripe's live mode
stripe.body: With live mode on in Stripe, add an endpoint with the same URL and the same events, and paste its secret into the live field under Integrations.

validate.title: Verify in production
validate.body: Repeat the verification with Test data off in the dashboard.

quickstart.title: Quickstart
quickstart.lead: Five steps to the first commission. Steps 1 and 2 are done once, whatever payment method you use.
quickstart.label: Quickstart steps

install.title: Install {brand}
install.body: Paste the tag in the {head} of every page of your site. Details under Tracking.

identify.title: Identify your customer
identify.body: When the visitor signs up, your server calls POST /api/identify. The referral then belongs to the customer — not to a checkout. Fields and responses under Customer identity.

connect.title: Connect a payment method
connect.body: Under Integrations → Payments → Add payment method, connect the account where your SaaS gets paid. You can connect more than one.
connect.label: Payment methods

test.title: Run a test
test.body: Open your site through a referral link, create a test account and pay in test mode. The full checklist is under Test the integration.

commission.title: See the commission
commission.body: The commission shows as Pending under Commissions. If it does not, the account's page shows where the payment stopped — see Payment without commission.

quickstart.oneIntegrationBody: Tracking and customer identity are independent of the payment method. Once {brand} is installed, you can connect as many billing accounts as you need — without redoing steps 1 and 2. See Multiple payment methods.

customerFirst.title: Recommended integration: customer-first
customerFirst.lead: For a SaaS where sign-up comes before billing, this is the recommended flow. The referral is linked to the customer when they create the account; from then on, the payment method only has to say who paid.
customerFirst.matchTitle: How each payment finds the customer
customerFirst.matchLead: {brand} looks for the first link that exists, in this order:

match.identity: The customer's id at the payment method, registered with identify (provider + providerCustomerId) — or already recorded by an earlier payment. Renewals use this path: no extra field.
match.metadata: Your own user id in the checkout metadata, when the method returns metadata (Stripe, Mercado Pago). See the Checkout Bridge.
match.reference: The attribution reference in the checkout, on any method: if its visitor was identified, the payment goes to that customer.
match.email: The e-mail sent to identify, when it matches exactly one identified customer of the same payment method. Customers are never merged by e-mail.

customerFirst.practice: If your backend creates the customer at the payment method during signup, send its id to identify and you are done. If the customer is only created by the payment method's checkout, add the Checkout Bridge fields — the same for any method.
customerFirst.rulesTitle: Switching payment methods does not change the program's rules
customerFirst.rulesBody: If the customer paid through Stripe and starts paying through another connected method, {brand} recognises the same customer and the same attribution. The commission is still subject to everything that already applied:

rules.window: The attribution window applies to the first commissioned payment; after it, only the duration decides.
rules.duration: The commission duration counts from the first commissioned payment, on any method — switching methods does not restart it.
rules.affiliate: The affiliate's participation must be approved at the time of payment.
rules.currency: The payment's currency must be the program's.
rules.environment: Test and live never mix: a test payment only reaches test programs.
rules.model: The attribution model (first or last click) decides which affiliate gets the customer at click time, not at payment.
rules.program: Pausing or archiving a program stops new attributions; customers already attributed keep following the rules above. See Paused program.

customerFirst.codeLead: The minimum code: in your sign-up, read the tracker's cookie and call identify. There is no SDK — it is a fetch call from your server.
customerFirst.codeNote: When you create the customer at the payment method, call again with the same externalId and the providerCustomerId: renewals are then recognised by it. All fields under Fields.

guestCheckout.title: Checkout without sign-up
guestCheckout.lead: If the purchase happens before we know who the customer is, the attribution reference has to travel to the checkout. That is the case for landing straight on a checkout, payment links and external checkouts.
guestCheckout.how: Which field carries the reference depends on the payment method — the table is under Checkout reference, and Stripe's samples under Stripe checkout reference. {brand} creates the customer from the payment and links the attribution to it; later renewals recognise it without a reference.

limits.first: A reference counts once: the first customer to use it keeps it. A forwarded link cannot credit someone else.
limits.expiry: The reference expires with the attribution window.
limits.none: With neither customer nor reference, the payment does not enter the commission ledger.

checkout.label: Checkout
checkout.note: you add the reference when you create the checkout

provider.label: Payment method
provider.note: keeps the reference with the payment

attribution.label: Attribution
attribution.note: the customer is created from the payment, with the affiliate

multipleProviders.title: Multiple payment methods
multipleProviders.lead: Tracking and customer identity are integrated once. Each payment method is just another connected account.
multipleProviders.example: Example: your SaaS uses Stripe for international cards, Mercado Pago for some local payments and AbacatePay for Pix.
multipleProviders.steps: Tick every method you use under Integrations → Overview. The ones left for later show as Optional and block nothing: one working method is enough for production.
multipleProviders.notTwice: You do not install {brand} three times.

diagram.label: One install, three billing accounts
diagram.description: {brand} is installed once and identifies the customer. Then Stripe, Mercado Pago and AbacatePay are connected; the same customer can pay through any of them, with one attribution and one commission rule.

multipleAccounts.title: Several accounts of the same method
multipleAccounts.lead: A company with Stripe in Brazil and in the US connects both accounts to the same workspace. Name each one when connecting, or rename it later.

items.workspace: Same workspace: the same programs, affiliates and commissions.
items.accounts: Separate accounts: each with its own name, status and diagnostics page.
items.events: Isolated events: what arrives from one account is never read as the other's, and test and live never mix.
items.identities: The same customer: your customer id is one; their id at each payment method is kept separately.

betaProviders.title: Payment methods in beta
betaProviders.lead: Mercado Pago, AbacatePay and Asaas are available inside the product as Beta.
betaProviders.meaning: This integration is being validated with real accounts. The architecture and the events are implemented and tested against the official documentation's payloads, but we recommend testing before using it in production. Beta is not “coming soon”: it works today, with monitoring.

mercado_pago.webhook: Manual, in the Mercado Pago panel

identityConcepts.title: Customer identity and billing identity
identityConcepts.lead: Two concepts that separate “who the customer is” from “how they pay”.

customer.name: Customer identity
customer.what: Your SaaS's customer, by your own user id. One per person, per environment.

billing.name: Billing identity
billing.what: That customer's id at a payment method (cus_… on Stripe, the payer on Mercado Pago…). A customer may have several, one per method.
billing.from: providerCustomerId in identify, or the first recognised payment.

identityConcepts.note: The payment method is part of the key: Stripe's customer 123 and Mercado Pago's 123 are different identities.

checkoutBridge.title: Checkout reference (Checkout Bridge)
checkoutBridge.lead: The fields that carry the attribution reference (and, optionally, your user id) to the checkout. {brand} picks the right field for each method: no names to memorise. There is no SDK to install — they are fields you add to the payload you already send.
checkoutBridge.where: Under Integrations → API → Checkout reference, {brand} shows the ready-made snippet for each method you connected.
checkoutBridge.betaNote: Beta methods: see each one's guide for an example payload.

missingCommission.title: Why did this payment not earn a commission?
missingCommission.lead: Each account's page, under Integrations → Payments, shows each payment's path under Diagnostics. Stop at the first pending step:

steps.referral: Referral — a referral link click created an attribution.
steps.customer: Customer identified — your server called identify for this customer.
steps.payment: Payment received — the payment method reported it and it entered the ledger.
steps.recognised: Customer recognised — the payment was linked to one of the customer's billing identities.
steps.eligible: Eligible attribution — the referral was valid on the payment date.
steps.commission: Commission created — the program's rules allowed it.

missingCommission.organic: A customer nobody referred shows as No referral, in grey. It is an organic sale — normal, and {brand} does not alert on it. The alert only appears when a referred customer pays and earns nothing.
missingCommission.reasonsLead: Under Activity, each event carries its exact reason in one sentence. The most common codes — the list is not exhaustive:
missingCommission.organicTitle: Not every payment has to earn a commission
missingCommission.whyTitle: Referred payment without commission: possible reasons

why.expired: Attribution expired — the first payment came after the attribution window.
why.affiliate: Affiliate inactive — the participation was not approved on the payment date.
why.environment: Wrong environment — a test payment never reaches a live program, and vice versa.
why.currency: Different currency — the payment is not in the program's currency.
why.duration: Past the duration — the recurring commission already served the program's term.
why.recognised: Customer not recognised — the payment carried no id, reference or e-mail linking it to the identified customer.
why.program: Program rule — for example, a click made while the program was paused creates no attribution. See Paused program.

providerCredentials.title: Payment method credentials
providerCredentials.lead: What {brand} keeps from each payment method, and how.

items.stripe: Stripe: no Stripe key at all. Through the (read-only) authorization or the endpoint signing secret (whsec_…).
items.encrypted: API keys and tokens (beta methods): encrypted with AES-256-GCM when saved, never shown again, never logged, deleted on disconnect.
items.dedicated: Prefer a dedicated key for {brand}: some methods have no read-only key.
items.secrets: The secrets that authenticate each connection's notifications are generated by {brand} and compared in constant time.
items.disconnect: Disconnecting stops new payments from the account; transactions and commissions already recorded are kept.

beta.title: Payment methods in beta
beta.lead: Mercado Pago, AbacatePay and Asaas are built and available inside the product as Beta. This page says exactly what each one does today — and what has not been validated yet.
beta.meaning: This integration is being validated with real accounts. The architecture and the events are implemented, and the contract is tested against the official documentation's payloads, but we recommend testing before using it in production. The connection's page shows every event and the reason behind each decision.

mercado_pago.connect: Under Integrations → Payments → Add payment method → Mercado Pago, paste your application's access token (APP_USR-… live, TEST-… test).
mercado_pago.automatic: Validates the token, generates this connection's notification URL, and fetches each notified payment straight from the Mercado Pago API.
mercado_pago.you: One manual step: Mercado Pago cannot register notifications by API. In the panel (Your integrations → your application → Webhooks), paste the URL {brand} shows, tick the topics below and paste back the secret signature. The connection only turns Healthy when the first verified notification arrives.
mercado_pago.refunds: Full and partial (the cumulative refunded amount becomes a proportional reversal). A chargeback (charged_back) reverses the commission.
mercado_pago.subscriptions: Yes, through subscriptions (preapproval) and their charges.
mercado_pago.environment: The environment comes from the token. One seller may hold a test and a live connection.
mercado_pago.limits: No OAuth yet (token pasted by hand). Payments made with test credentials send no notifications. A won dispute does not restore the commission automatically.
mercado_pago.test: Use the webhook simulator in the Mercado Pago panel, or a small real payment.

abacatepay.automatic: {brand} sets up the webhook automatically after validating your key, with a secret unique to this connection.
abacatepay.you: Nothing in the panel. Carry the reference to the checkout (externalId → see the Checkout Bridge) or identify the customer.
abacatepay.refunds: Full refunds only (AbacatePay has no partial refund). An opened dispute reverses the commission.
abacatepay.subscriptions: Yes: first charge, renewals and cancellation.
abacatepay.environment: The environment comes from the key (dev mode = test).
abacatepay.limits: AbacatePay does not return metadata in its webhooks: your user id must arrive through identify. There is no dispute-won event, so a reversed commission does not come back by itself.
abacatepay.test: Use an abc_dev_ key and buy in dev mode.

asaas.connect: Paste an API key ($aact_prod_…, or $aact_hmlg_… for the sandbox).
asaas.automatic: {brand} sets up the webhook automatically after validating your key, with a token unique to this connection, and removes it when you disconnect.
asaas.you: Nothing in the panel. Use a key dedicated to {brand}: Asaas has no read-only key and disables keys unused for 3 months.
asaas.refunds: Full and partial. A chargeback request reverses the commission.
asaas.subscriptions: Yes: each cycle is a payment linked to the subscription.
asaas.environment: Sandbox and live are separate Asaas accounts: each one is a connection.
asaas.limits: Asaas does not sign notifications with HMAC: authentication is the connection's own token. There is no metadata: your user id must arrive through identify.
asaas.test: Use a sandbox key and pay a test charge in the sandbox.

beta.notComingSoon: Beta is not “coming soon”: a beta method works today and can be connected. “Coming soon” is a method that is not available yet.
beta.statusValue: Implemented, tested against official payloads, not yet fully validated with a real account.

report.title: How to report a problem
report.lead: Open the account under Integrations → Payments. Advanced settings hold the details that help investigate. When reporting, include:

items.event: the last event (type) and roughly when it arrived;
items.when: what you expected to happen — for example, “a $49.00 payment with no commission”.

report.never: API keys, access tokens and signing secrets are not needed to investigate. If one leaked, create a new one at the payment method and save it on the account's page.

refunds.title: Refunds and disputes
refunds.lead: A refund never deletes or edits a commission. It creates a reversal — a negative row pointing at the original — so the history stays complete.

full.result: The whole commission is reversed. If it was not paid yet, it becomes Reversed.

partial.result: A reversal proportional to the amount returned, adding up earlier refunds. It is netted with the original commission in the batch.

dispute.result: Reverses the commission like a refund.

disputeWon.result: Stripe only: the reversed amount comes back as Pending and serves the hold period again.

refunds.paidBody: If the commission was already paid to the affiliate, {brand} records the reversal but does not claw it back or deduct it from the next batch — there is no automatic clawback yet. Settle the difference with the affiliate directly, if you want.
refunds.providers: Beta methods differ: AbacatePay only has full refunds, and no beta method restores a commission after a won dispute. Details under Beta payment methods.

integrationHealth.title: Integration health
integrationHealth.lead: Each connected account shows a status under Integrations. It comes from what actually arrived — connected is not the same as working.

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.meaning: Payments arrive, find their customers, and referred customers earn commissions.

configuring.name: Setting up
configuring.meaning: A step only you can do is pending, such as the notifications in the Mercado Pago panel.
configuring.action: Follow the steps on the account's page.

awaiting.name: Waiting for events
awaiting.meaning: Everything is set up; the account has not sent a payment yet.

degraded.name: Needs attention
degraded.meaning: Working, with a warning: no event for days, events from the wrong environment, or a referred customer who paid without earning a commission.
degraded.action: Read the warning on the account's page.

actionRequired.name: Action required
actionRequired.meaning: Something stops it from working: a refused credential, rejected notifications or payments without a customer.
actionRequired.action: Fix it on the page itself — for example, by saving a new key.

error.name: Error
error.meaning: The last event received was not processed.
error.action: The payment method retries by itself. If it persists, see Activity.

disconnected.name: Disconnected
disconnected.meaning: Nothing new arrives from this account. Transactions and commissions are preserved.

setupIncomplete.name: Setup incomplete
setupIncomplete.meaning: You started the manual setup and did not finish it — for example, you entered the Stripe account and have not pasted the secret yet.
setupIncomplete.action: Open the account and click Continue setup: it resumes at the missing step.

integrationHealth.notErrorTitle: A state is not a problem
integrationHealth.notErrorBody: Waiting for the first event is not an error. Notifications still to set up is a pending action. An invalid credential is a problem. A rejected notification is an error. The account's page keeps these four apart.
integrationHealth.advancedLead: Behind each payment's path there are six records. Useful when you need to check a case through the API or the ids under Advanced settings.

attribution.name: Attribution
attribution.what: Links a referred visitor to a program's affiliate, with an expiry (the window).

customer.name: Customer
customer.what: Your SaaS's customer, by your id (externalId), one per environment.

billingIdentity.name: Billing Identity
billingIdentity.what: That customer's id at a payment method (cus_… on Stripe). A customer can have several.

billingEvent.name: Billing Event
billingEvent.what: A notification received from a connected account, with its outcome and reason (Activity).

transaction.name: Transaction
transaction.what: A payment, refund or dispute in the ledger, in minor units with its currency.

commission.name: Commission
commission.what: What the affiliate is owed for a transaction, with the rule applied. Refunds create reversals.

webhookSecurity.title: Webhook security
webhookSecurity.lead: How {brand} decides whether a payment notification can be trusted.

items.verified: Verified before it is read: by the payment method's signature or by a secret exclusive to each connection, compared in constant time.
items.rejected: Refused with no effect: a notification that fails verification records nothing.
items.once: Processed once: redeliveries of the same event answer success without redoing anything.
items.environment: Test and live isolated: a test event on a live connection (or the reverse) is ignored.
items.token: Opaque reference: ifx_… is random, carries no customer data and cannot be guessed.
items.customer: Your id only comes from your server: through identify with the secret key, or the metadata of the checkout your backend creates — never from a field the browser controls.

saasAffiliateProgram.metaDescription: SaaS affiliate software that tracks referrals, attributes customers, pays recurring commissions from Stripe and reverses refunds. No cut of your revenue.
saasAffiliateProgram.title: Affiliate software for SaaS
saasAffiliateProgram.lead: An affiliate program pays partners for the customers they send you. In SaaS the sale is a subscription, so the commission has to follow every renewal, upgrade and refund. Here is what SaaS affiliate software has to handle, and how {brand} does it.
saasAffiliateProgram.ctaSecondary: See how it works with Stripe

what.title: What SaaS affiliate software does
what.p1: It runs the program your SaaS offers to partners — consultants, agencies, creators in your niche, happy customers — who recommend your product and earn a commission on each paying customer they bring. You are the company running the program, not a publisher promoting someone else's store.
what.p2: What makes SaaS different is time. The sale does not end at checkout: the customer pays every month, upgrades, asks for a refund or disputes a charge months later. Each of those events changes what the affiliate is owed.

when.title: When an affiliate program fits
when.p1: Affiliate programs work best when customers sign up on their own and revenue repeats. Four signals:

recurring.title: Your revenue is recurring
recurring.body: A commission on the first months costs less than what the customer is worth over the subscription.

partners.title: People already recommend you
partners.body: Consultants and creators in your niche already suggest tools. A program makes it official and gives them a reason to keep going.

selfServe.title: You sell self-serve
selfServe.body: When customers sign up on your site, a link can follow the path from click to payment.

results.title: You want to pay for results only
results.body: A commission is a variable cost: it exists only after a customer has paid.

when.note: If every deal goes through months of sales calls, individual partner agreements usually work better than referral links.

tracking.title: Affiliate tracking
tracking.p1: It starts with a link such as yoursaas.com/?ref=marina. A script on your site reads the affiliate's code, keeps a visitor id in a cookie on your own domain and records the click.
tracking.p2: The hard part comes later: visitors rarely sign up on the first visit. They come back days later by typing your URL. So the click stays valid for an attribution window — in {brand}, anywhere from 1 to 365 days, set per program.

attribution.title: Attribution: who earns the commission
attribution.p1: When two affiliates refer the same person, something has to decide who wins. The common rules are first click (who introduced the product) and last click (who closed it). {brand} applies whichever rule you pick for the program.
attribution.p2: Once a customer is tied to an affiliate, renewals stay with that affiliate: a new click from someone else does not take over a subscription that already exists.

recurring.title: Recurring commissions
recurring.p1: SaaS programs typically pay a percentage of each invoice for a period — say 30% for the first 12 months — or for as long as the customer stays. A fixed amount per customer works too.
recurring.p2: Every paid invoice produces its own commission, stored with the rule that produced it. A hold period of 0 to 180 days keeps a commission from becoming payable right away, which leaves time for a refund to show up.

refunds.title: Refunds and chargebacks
refunds.p1: If a customer is refunded or disputes the charge, the commission on that payment should not be paid. {brand} receives those events from Stripe and records a reversal — the original commission is never deleted, so the history still adds up. If you win the dispute, the commission comes back.
refunds.p2: If the commission was already paid out, the reversal stays on record for you to settle with the affiliate; {brand} does not deduct it from future payouts on its own.

stripe.title: Payments from Stripe
stripe.p1: A commission comes from a confirmed payment, not from a form someone filled in. With Stripe, confirmation arrives as a signed webhook and each event is processed exactly once — a retry never pays a commission twice.
stripe.p2: It works with Stripe Checkout, Payment Links, custom checkouts (PaymentIntent) and the Subscriptions API. The details are in <stripe>Stripe affiliate software</stripe>.

portal.title: Affiliate portal
portal.p1: Affiliates who cannot see their numbers email you to ask. In the portal, each affiliate signs in with their own account and follows their links, conversions, commissions and payouts — theirs only.

payouts.title: Payouts and reconciliation
payouts.p1: At the end of the period there is one question: how much do I owe, and to whom? {brand} groups payable commissions into a payout batch, exports it as CSV and records what you marked as paid.
payouts.p2: The money leaves your account through whatever method you already use. {brand} never moves payments.

simulate.body: No code, no Stripe: watch a click become a commission through the same engine that calculates real ones.

install.title: Install the tracker
install.body: One tag on your site. With Payment Links that is all; other checkouts need one extra field.

connect.title: Connect Stripe
connect.body: Payments start producing commissions. To process real money, turn on a paid plan.

invite.title: Invite affiliates
invite.body: Each one gets their own link and access to the portal.

start.note: {brand} charges a fixed monthly fee, with no percentage of the revenue your affiliates bring in. See the <pricing>plans</pricing>.

marketplace.question: Is this for people who want to become affiliates?
marketplace.answer: No. {brand} is for the company running the program: you create an affiliate program for your own SaaS and pay the partners who bring you customers.

rate.question: What commission should I offer?
rate.answer: It depends on your margin and on what a customer is worth over the subscription. A common starting point is a percentage of the monthly fee for a limited period. In {brand} each commission keeps the rule that produced it, so changing the rule never rewrites what was already calculated.

developer.question: Do I need a developer?
developer.answer: Not to try it: Sandbox simulates a conversion without code. For production, someone pastes one tag on your site and, depending on your checkout, adds one field where the charge is created. With Payment Links, just the tag.

money.question: Does {brand} pay my affiliates for me?
money.answer: No. It calculates, records and shows what you owe each affiliate, and you pay them however you prefer. No money passes through {brand}.

fee.question: Do you take a percentage of my revenue?
fee.answer: No. You pay a fixed monthly fee for the tool. There is no fee on attributed revenue and no revenue cap.

closing.title: Set up your SaaS affiliate program
closing.body: Start in Sandbox — free, no card — and see your first commission calculated before you touch your checkout.

affiliateSoftware.metaDescription: Spreadsheet, in-house build or affiliate management software? Compare tracking, recurring commissions, refunds and the affiliate portal. Fixed price.
affiliateSoftware.title: Affiliate management software for SaaS
affiliateSoftware.lead: Every affiliate program starts in a spreadsheet. It holds up until the first renewal, the first refund or the second affiliate claiming the same customer. Here is what changes between staying on the spreadsheet, building it in-house and using affiliate management software.

options.title: Three ways to run the program

table.caption: Spreadsheet, in-house build and affiliate software compared task by task

tracking.spreadsheet: The affiliate tells you who they sent
tracking.inHouse: You build the script, cookie and endpoint
tracking.software: A ready script and one link per affiliate

attribution.inHouse: A rule to write and test
attribution.software: First or last click, with a window

portal.inHouse: One more logged-in area to maintain
portal.software: A portal with links and commissions

spreadsheet.title: When a spreadsheet is still enough
spreadsheet.p1: With a handful of affiliates and a one-time commission per sale, a spreadsheet works. It stops working when commissions recur — every renewal becomes a new row — and when a refund has to undo a commission that already sits in someone's balance.

inHouse.title: The hidden cost of building it yourself
inHouse.p1: A link with ?ref= looks like an afternoon of work. The real system is cookies and an attribution window, tie-breaking between affiliates, Stripe webhooks without duplicates, a commission per invoice, reversals on refunds and chargebacks, reconciliation of what was paid, and a portal for affiliates.
inHouse.p2: It is financial infrastructure: a bug means overpaid commissions or unhappy partners. And it has to stay correct every time Stripe changes its API.

criteria.title: What to look for in affiliate management software

tracking.title: Tracking that survives checkout
tracking.body: The link between click and payment has to reach Stripe, without relying on the customer using the same email.

recurring.title: Commissions per invoice, not per sale
recurring.body: A subscription earns every month; the commission should follow each paid invoice and stop when the period ends.

reversals.title: Refunds that reverse
reversals.body: Refunds and chargebacks should produce reversals without erasing history.

ledger.title: An auditable history
ledger.body: Each commission should show the rule, the payment and the affiliate behind it.

pricing.title: Pricing that does not grow with your revenue
pricing.body: Some platforms take a percentage of the revenue affiliates bring in: the better the program, the bigger the bill.

test.title: A test environment
test.body: The ability to simulate a conversion before real money is involved.

product.title: How {brand} handles it
product.p1: {brand} is affiliate management software for SaaS companies that bill through Stripe. A script records the click, an attribution reference follows the visitor into checkout, Stripe's webhook confirms the payment, and the commission engine calculates and records it.

rules.title: Rules per program
rules.body: Percentage or fixed amount, recurring for months or for life, attribution window and hold period. On Growth, a custom rate per affiliate.

environments.title: Test and live kept apart
environments.body: Test and live programs never mix. Sandbox is free and does not expire.

portal.title: Affiliate portal
portal.body: Each affiliate sees their own links, conversions, commissions and payouts.

payouts.title: Payout batches
payouts.body: Group what is payable, export CSV and record what was paid.

privacy.title: Customer data protected
privacy.body: Customer emails are stored as hashes, never in plain text.

custody.title: No custody
custody.body: {brand} never moves money: you pay affiliates from your own account.

pricingModel.title: Pricing model
pricingModel.p1: A fixed monthly fee per plan, billed in Brazilian reais (BRL). No percentage of attributed revenue and no revenue cap: plan limits cover programs, affiliates and team members, never revenue. See <pricing>pricing</pricing>.

checkout.question: Do I have to replace my checkout?
checkout.answer: No. You keep Stripe Checkout, Payment Links or your own Stripe-based checkout. What changes is one reference when the charge is created — and with Payment Links, not even that.

withoutStripe.question: Does it work without Stripe?
withoutStripe.answer: Not today. Commissions are calculated from Stripe payments; if you bill some other way, {brand} is not the right tool yet.

limits.question: Is there a revenue or commission limit?
limits.answer: No. Plans limit programs, affiliates and team members. Revenue and the number of commissions are uncapped.

trial.question: Can I try it before paying?
trial.answer: Yes. Sandbox is free, needs no card and does not expire, with test data. You only subscribe to process real payments.

closing.title: Replace the spreadsheet with a real affiliate system
closing.body: Set up the program in Sandbox and see a commission calculated end to end before you connect real payments.

stripeAffiliates.metaDescription: Track affiliates on Stripe payments: Checkout, Payment Links, custom checkouts and subscriptions. Recurring commissions, refund reversals, no secret key.
stripeAffiliates.title: Affiliate software for SaaS on Stripe
stripeAffiliates.lead: If your SaaS bills through Stripe, every payment already passes through one place. {brand} ties the affiliate's click to that payment and calculates the commission from what Stripe confirms — invoice by invoice.

click.title: Click
click.body: The visitor arrives through the affiliate's link. The tracker records the click and keeps an attribution reference in the browser.

checkout.title: Checkout
checkout.body: The reference travels to Stripe with the charge: as client_reference_id on Checkout, or in metadata.

webhook.title: Webhook
webhook.body: Stripe reports the confirmed payment. The event arrives signed and is processed exactly once.

commission.title: Commission
commission.body: The commission is calculated with the program's rule and recorded with the payment that produced it.

methods.title: Supported ways to charge

table.caption: What changes in your code for each Stripe payment method

checkout.setup: Pass the reference as client_reference_id when you create the session.

paymentLinks.setup: Nothing beyond the tag: the tracker appends the reference to the buy.stripe.com links on your page.

subscriptions.setup: Send the reference in the subscription's metadata, once. Renewals follow.

other.setup: Your backend calls POST /api/identify to tie the visitor to the customer.

methods.note: You can use more than one at once. Each is walked through step by step in the <docs>documentation</docs>.

recurring.title: Subscriptions and recurring commissions
recurring.p1: Every paid invoice on a subscription produces that cycle's commission, for as long as the recurrence you set — a few months or for life. A percentage commission follows the amount actually paid on each invoice.
recurring.p2: The customer stays with the affiliate who brought them: a new click from another affiliate does not change who earns on renewals.

refunds.title: Refunds and disputes
refunds.p1: A refund or a dispute on Stripe reverses the commission tied to that payment. If you win the dispute, the commission comes back. Nothing is deleted: every correction is a new record in the history.

security.title: No access to your money
security.p1: {brand} only reads events. During setup you enter your account ID and the webhook signing secret (whsec_…) — never your API secret key. {brand} does not charge, transfer or pay out anything on your account.

testMode.title: Test before going live
testMode.p1: Stripe test-mode events go to test programs; live events go to live programs. Validate the whole flow with Stripe's test cards — or simulate a conversion in Sandbox without Stripe at all.

secretKey.question: Do I have to share my Stripe secret key?
secretKey.answer: No. {brand} receives events by webhook and verifies each one with the endpoint's signing secret. Your account's secret key stays with you.

checkout.question: Do I have to change my checkout?
checkout.answer: It depends on how you charge. Payment Links: no. Stripe Checkout: one field when creating the session. Custom checkout or Subscriptions API: one metadata key.

events.question: Which Stripe events are used?
events.answer: Paid invoices, one-off payments, completed checkouts, refunds, disputes and subscription changes. The full list is in the <docs>documentation</docs>.

payouts.question: Does {brand} pay affiliates through Stripe?
payouts.answer: No. {brand} calculates and records what you owe; affiliates are paid from your account, through the method you choose.

closing.title: Connect your affiliates to your Stripe payments
closing.body: Create the program in Sandbox, simulate a conversion and connect Stripe when you are ready.

terms.lead: These terms apply to anyone who creates a {brand} account or uses the affiliate portal. By creating your account, you agree to them.

service.title: What {brand} is
paragraphs: {brand} is software for SaaS companies to run their affiliate programs. It records clicks on referral links, links each referral to the customer who signs up, reads the payments reported by the payment methods you connect, and calculates and records commissions under your program's rules.
“You” is the person or company that creates an account and manages a workspace; “affiliates” are the people you invite to promote your product.

account.title: Your account
paragraphs: To use {brand} you create an account with an e-mail and a password. You are responsible for the information you provide, for keeping your password secret, and for everything that happens in your account and in the workspaces you manage, including actions by members you invite.
Your workspace's API keys give access to your data: keep the secret key on your server and create a new one if you suspect a leak.

program.title: Your affiliate program
paragraphs: You set your program's rules — commission, duration, attribution window, hold period — and decide which affiliates to approve. The relationship with your affiliates is yours: {brand} is not a party to the agreements between you and them.

You are responsible for telling your affiliates the program's rules, for obtaining whatever is needed to process their data and your customers' data, and for complying with the laws that apply to your program, including data-protection and consumer-protection law.

money.title: {brand} does not move commission money
paragraphs: {brand} tracks, attributes, calculates and records commissions. It does not receive, hold or transfer money to affiliates. You pay commissions yourself, through the method you choose; {brand} only records what you report as paid.
Calculated amounts depend on the data sent by payment methods and on your integration. Check the amounts before you pay.

providers.title: Payment methods and third-party services
paragraphs: To recognise sales, {brand} connects to the billing accounts you authorise, such as Stripe. Your use of those services follows their own terms, between you and them. {brand} reads the payment events it needs and does not charge anyone on your billing account.

Integrations marked Beta are being validated: they work, but we recommend monitoring the results before relying on them alone. An integration may stop working if the third party changes or suspends its service.

subscription.title: Your {brand} subscription
paragraphs: You can use the free plan for testing. Paid plans are billed monthly, at the prices and limits published on the pricing page. Subscription billing is processed by Stripe.
You can cancel at any time; cancelling stops the following renewals. Taxes, where applicable, follow the law in force.

acceptableUse.title: Acceptable use

process people's data without a legal basis or against the law;
try to access other workspaces' data, get around limits or security controls, or overload the service;
promote illegal or misleading products or content, or content that infringes others' rights;

availability.title: Availability

suspension.title: Suspension and termination

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lead: This policy explains what personal data {brand} processes, why, who it is shared with and how you can exercise your rights.

roles.title: Who decides about each piece of data
paragraphs: For your account data and our website, {brand} decides how and why it is processed.

For the data you put into {brand} about your program — affiliates, visitors to your site, your customers and their payments — {brand} processes it on behalf of the SaaS company using the service, following its instructions. If you are an affiliate or a customer of one of those companies, send requests about that data to the company first; {brand} helps it answer them.

account.title: Your account data
paragraphs: When you create an account or are invited to a workspace, we process:
items: name, e-mail and password (the password is kept by our authentication provider in protected form and is never visible to us);
workspaces, roles and invitations;
records of administrative actions (for example, connecting or disconnecting a payment method), for security and auditing;
your plan and subscription status. Card details are handled by Stripe, not by {brand}.

customerData.title: Data {brand} processes for your program
paragraphs: To track, attribute and calculate commissions, {brand} processes:
items: Affiliates: the name, e-mail, company and country provided, referral links and codes.

Referred visitors: a random visitor identifier, the address of the landing page and of the referring page, UTM parameters, device type, approximate country and a hash of the IP address — the IP itself is not stored.
The SaaS's customers: the customer's id in the SaaS's system and at the payment methods, and the e-mail only as a hash, used to recognise the same customer.
Payments: amounts, currency, dates, refunds and disputes received from connected payment methods, and the commissions calculated from them.
Payment-method notifications: the id, type and outcome of each event. The full content of notifications is not stored.
Integration credentials: keys and tokens of connected payment methods, stored encrypted and never shown again.

website.title: Our website
paragraphs: On our own site we use few cookies: those needed for sign-in and security, preferences such as language, and a visit-origin cookie (channel and landing page, no personal identifier) that is not set when the browser asks not to be tracked. Details in the <cookies>Cookie Policy</cookies>. We use no third-party advertising or analytics tools.

use.title: What we use data for
items: providing the service: authentication, tracking referrals, recognising payments and calculating commissions;
keeping the service secure, preventing fraud and abuse, and investigating incidents;
billing the {brand} subscription;
understanding, in aggregate, how people reach our site and use the product, to improve it;
meeting legal obligations and answering authorities when required.

sharing.title: Who we share data with
paragraphs: We do not sell personal data. We share data only with providers needed to run the service, who process it under our instructions:
items: database and authentication provider (Supabase), including for sign-in and invitation e-mails;
hosting and delivery provider (Vercel);
Stripe, for billing the {brand} subscription;
the payment methods the SaaS itself connects (such as the company's Stripe), from which {brand} reads the authorised payment events;
authorities, when the law requires.

security.title: Security
paragraphs: Data travels over encrypted connections. Integration credentials are encrypted before being stored; API keys, customer e-mails and IP addresses are stored only as hashes. Access to each workspace's data is restricted to its members by rules enforced in the database itself, and system logs do not include passwords, keys or tokens.
No system is entirely immune to failures. If an incident may affect you, we will notify you as the law requires.

retention.title: How long we keep data
paragraphs: We keep data while the account or workspace exists and as needed to provide the service. The financial history — payments, commissions and reversals — is kept as a record and is not deleted when a payment method is disconnected. When an account is deleted, its data is removed or anonymised, except what the law requires us to keep. Cookie durations are in the <cookies>Cookie Policy</cookies>.

rights.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Under the applicable law, such as Brazil's LGPD, you may ask for:
items: confirmation that we process your data, and access to it;
correction of incomplete or outdated data;
anonymisation, blocking or deletion of unnecessary data or data processed unlawfully;
portability, and information about who we share data with;
review of decisions and objection to processing, where the law provides.

international.title: International transfers
paragraphs: Some of the providers listed above may process data outside Brazil. In those cases, we require them to protect the data adequately.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We may update this policy. The date at the top shows the current version; relevant changes will be announced with reasonable notice.

cookies.title: Cookie Policy
cookies.lead: Cookies are small files your browser keeps. This page lists every one {brand} uses, what it is for and how long it lasts.

what.title: How we use cookies
paragraphs: We sort cookies into three kinds: necessary (the service does not work without them, such as sign-in), functional (they remember choices such as language) and measurement (understanding where visits come from). We use no advertising or third-party cookies.

site.title: On the {brand} site and dashboard
paragraphs: These live on {brand}'s domain. The session cookie is created by our authentication provider and may be split into parts sharing the same prefix.

customerSite.title: On our customers' sites (tracker)
paragraphs: Companies using {brand} install a tracker on their own site. It sets these cookies on the company's domain to remember that the visitor came through a referral link. They hold no direct personal data: a random identifier and a random reference.
Each company is responsible for informing its visitors and, where required, obtaining consent for these cookies on its own site.

choices.title: Your choices
paragraphs: You can delete or block cookies in your browser settings; without the necessary ones, sign-in stops working. If your browser sends the Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track signal, {brand} does not set the visit-origin measurement cookie.

changes.title: Changes
